title: Redwood June 2026 Leadership Update
transcript:
Header: Redwood Inference - June 2026 Leadership Update
Date/Time: 2026-06-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir, Lena, Maria, Diego, Naomi, Aaron + company-wide

Summary: Quick leadership updates across product, eng, sales, research; Q2 metrics and hiring cadence; security/SOC2 progress; Dedicated customer highlights; nods to cost/perf wins and roadmap priorities. Q&A and next steps at the end.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off in a couple minutes while folks filter in. um, quick note, we're recording this for folks in APAC.
[00:24] Samir: All right, let's get started. high level: Q2 is shaping up pretty well, we hit the committed throughput targets on Dedicated, and our hosted latency p95 went down about 18% month over month. big shoutout to infra and runtime teams.
[00:45] Lena: yeah real quick, the kernel selection changes and the batching improvements landed last sprint. there are still a couple edge cases on very long-context chat where the kv cache - uh, the "kay vee cache" - still has some misses, but we're seeing stable gains across the board.
[01:10] Diego: yep and the autoscaler improvements reduced tail latency spikes during bursts, which helped with a couple big weekends for customers. small hiccup with one of the regions, we had a networking flap in eu-west-2 that caused a short degradation; that postmortem is in T-Docs.
[01:36] Maria: product update: we shipped streaming function calling in beta for hosted customers and the response has been positive. adoption is at ~12% of text-gen requests for new customers and conversion from the trial has been higher for teams using streaming.
[02:00] Naomi: on the research side, we onboarded two new open model variants that are performing well under our quantization profiles; this helps on cost per token with minimal quality regression for retrieval-heavy workloads.
[02:25] Aaron: Sales highlights: closed two mid-market deals this month on Dedicated capacity, one financial services which required the VPC private deployment plus additional audit logs. procurement timeline was about 6 weeks from initial scoping to signed contract.
[02:48] Samir: good. quick numbers: ARR growth this quarter is +21% QoQ, gross margin improving as we tune inference cost. we're still watching CAC - acquisition cost - for hosted; marketing and product are collaborating on more self-serve flows to reduce friction.
[03:12] Lena: on reliability, we shipped an internal tracing hook that surfaces per-route model fallback frequency. this allowed ops to identify a model-mismatch that hit a large customer, and we pushed a canary rollback quickly.
[03:36] Diego: engineering hiring update: we're targeting 18 hires this quarter across infra, runtime, and platform. we're trending slightly behind plan due to competing offers in the market; recruiter pipeline is improving but need interview throughput.
[03:57] Samir: earmarked more budget for contractor-to-hire conversions and interview de-risking. we'll share a hiring playbook later this week.
[04:12] Maria: roadmap priorities next 90 days: 1) complete private control plane GA for a pilot customer, 2) expand model catalog with two additional Redwood-verified models, 3) UX improvements for the console cost breakdowns.
[04:35] Naomi: research will focus on a model pruning experiment and a quantization library that better preserves embeddings quality at 4-bit for production embedding workloads.
[04:52] Aaron: also pushing channel partnerships in APAC - partner pilots with a cloud reseller went live last month; early signal looks promising but we need support from Solutions on a localized pricing deck.
[05:10] Samir: security/compliance update - we are on track for SOC 2 Type 2 readiness in Q3. security team completed encryption-in-transit verification and we've integrated KMS for private deployments. still working on automated audit exports for the console.
[05:34] Lena: small note: SSO/SAML flows have a bug where group syncs from Okta don't always map to our RBAC roles, causing a support ticket spike. fix is slotted for next sprint.
[05:52] Samir: Customers: we highlighted one Dedicated customer who reduced per-token cost by 30% after moving from single model hosted pipeline to a mixed quantized stack in Dedicated. Diego's team ran a benchmark session and captured the numbers.
[06:12] Diego: yep, shared bench sheet in #benchmarks; it's approximate but helped finance justify the Dedicated commit. also we saw an interesting tradeoff: latency increased slightly for very short prompts but Avg cost dropped materially.
[06:35] (crosstalk)
[06:50] Samir: Pricing/packaging: Finance completed an analysis of committed vs burst pricing. our recommendation - and we'll trial this with a couple customers - is to offer a 10% discount on 12-month Dedicated commits with a burst pool option capped at 25% of baseline.
[07:12] Maria: product needs a UI for the burst policy and cost simulator, that's on the backlog.
[07:26] Naomi: research question - we should add metric for embedding drift; teams have reported subtle quality regressions when switching quantization profiles.
[07:40] Lena: agreed, add to metrics dashboard.
[07:48] Samir: Ops/infra note: plan to deprecate the old docker-based runtime images by end of Q3; want to give teams heads-up for migration.
[08:05] Diego: migration tooling will be ready mid-July; we'll run a migration canary with a staging customer.
[08:18] Aaron: sales ramp: need updated battlecards vs competitor offerings. current competitor chatter: OpenAI pricing moves, Anthropic enterprise bundles, and some self-host vendors promoting lower-cost on-prem alternatives.
[08:38] Samir: good, competitive intelligence please centralize in the saleswiki.
[08:46] (long pause as chat participants join)
[09:03] Employee question (Q): is there an update on the private deployment licensing model?
[09:10] Maria: yes, core is a platform license + per-node usage for on-prem; for VPC we have a service fee plus per-request usage. pricing details will be in the next partner package we circulate.
[09:26] Q: will we support HSM for KMS in the private package?
[09:30] Lena: yes HSM integrations are in the roadmap; a couple customers require it and we're prioritizing.
[09:38] Samir: ok next: org health. we're tracking engagement up slightly month over month; pulse survey goes out Friday. hiring churn is okay but we need to move faster on senior infra ICs.
[09:56] Diego: retention initiatives - mentorship program and comp refresh for high performers, budget approved for Q3.
[10:10] Samir: finance briefly - net burn improved vs forecast; runway extended by 2 quarters based on conservative growth modeling. we still need to balance invest vs runway; leadership will meet offline on allocations.
[10:30] Naomi: research publishable wins - a new inference technique we prototyped decreased KV cache overhead by ~12% in internal evals; we plan to open-source a reproducible benchmark later this quarter.
[10:48] Aaron: customer success highlight - a renewal for a large ed-tech customer closed with an expansion; they cited dashboard clarity and predictable latency as main reasons.
[11:05] Samir: good. questions?
[11:12] Employee (Jules): can we get more transparency on model roadmap - which models will be Redwood-verified?
[11:18] Maria: we'll publish a model roadmap snapshot next Tuesday with verification criteria and expected timeline.
[11:26] Employee (Anita): any news on office space / return-to-office policy?
[11:30] Samir: hybrid remains; team leads will communicate local expectations, HR will share guidelines.
[11:37] (brief side conversation)
[11:50] Samir: quick closing recap: 1) hiring playbook and budget adjustments - Samir/Diego, due 2026-06-17; 2) model roadmap snapshot - Maria, due 2026-06-16; 3) SOC 2 artifacts and audit export plan - Lena/Security, due 2026-06-30; 4) migration tooling and deprecation schedule - Diego, mid-July canary; 5) publish bench results and cost-savings case study - Diego/Aaron, due 2026-06-24.
[12:30] Maria: also reminder: all-hands survey Friday, please fill it out.
[12:40] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll post the recording and deck. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription with minor speaker attribution errors and occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "kay vee" for KV cache).
next_steps: Publish deck and recording to Confluence
Share hiring playbook and interview de-risk plan
Run migration canary for runtime deprecation

Lena - complete SOC 2 audit export plan - 2026-06-30
